planHint: Only managed resources are listed. Secret file contents are never shown.
noSelection: Select a connection to shape its route.
notMonitored: Last deployment status; not a continuous uptime monitor.
connectBatchHint: Select at least one entry and one exit. A connection editor will apply the same settings to each pair.
destinationRequired: Your destination service must already be running. MeshDock installs tunnel infrastructure only.
serverChangedTrust: Changing the SSH endpoint requires a new fingerprint check.

caveats.private_tls: Pinned private TLS; this is not browser camouflage.
caveats.udp_required: Requires UDP. Salamander cannot overcome a blanket UDP block.

controlPortHint: Optional {{protocol}} port, such as 443. Must be free on the receiving server. Leave empty for an automatic port.
exclusionHint: Comma-separated ports or ranges inside the entry range. Remaining target offsets stay unchanged.
nativeRangeMode: Compact ranges · TCP via HAProxy, UDP via kernel forwarding
expandedRangeMode: Individual transport listeners · capacity checked on the server
mappingPlatform: Supported hosts: Debian / Ubuntu, systemd, IPv4. Choose TCP, UDP or both per range, subject to transport support.
invalidRange: Enter a port or an ascending range from 1 to 65535, for example 8000-8099.
rangeWidth: Entry and target ranges must contain the same number of ports.
invalidExclusions: Exceptions must be inside the entry range, without duplicates or overlaps (maximum 128 items).
emptyMapping: At least one port must remain after exceptions.
mappingOverlap: Mapping rows overlap. Split the ranges or add explicit exceptions.
mappingSshConflict: This range includes the entry server’s SSH port. Exclude it to preserve access.
mappingLimit: This mapping exceeds this method’s port space ({{max}}). Check the ranges and exceptions.
actualPortConflicts: No blanket reserved port range. Topology conflicts are checked on save; live server listeners are checked before deployment.
nativePoolHint: GRE ranges must be exclusive on this entry. Shared-port load balancing is available for individual GRE ports and other methods.
nativeHealthHint: Checks verify the GRE peer and every HAProxy listener, not every destination service. Large ranges need enough file descriptors and explicit exclusions for outgoing ports.
socketCapacityHint: Each mapped port needs a public listener and a private transport listener. Large ranges use more memory and file descriptors; they do not guarantee more speed.
sshSessionCount_one: {{count}} SSH session · up to {{size}} forwards per session
sshSessionCount_other: {{count}} SSH sessions · up to {{size}} forwards per session
rangeHealthHint: Ranges check all tunnel listeners, not every destination service. You can start services later. Pool health samples the transport; it does not detect individual destination outages.
resourcePlan: {{count}} planned listening sockets · per-process file limit {{nofile}} · estimated descriptor budget {{budget}}. Live limits are checked before deployment; memory and throughput still depend on the server.
outgoingPortHint: The server also needs free ports for outgoing TCP connections. If a large range consumes that space on its egress IP, deployment asks for explicit exceptions or a separate ingress IP.

advanced.title: Advanced settings
advanced.deployHint: Changes apply when you save. Both ends are updated; active connections may reconnect.
advanced.switchHint: Each method keeps its own draft while this panel is open. Only the selected method’s settings are saved.
advanced.invalid: Check numeric limits and dependent settings. Buffer sizes must fit their parent buffer, and heartbeat/keepalive intervals must be shorter than their timeout.

methods.backhaul: TCP, UDP, TCPMUX, WS, WSS, WSMUX and WSSMUX. TCP supports TCP/UDP mappings; native UDP supports UDP only. TLS modes use a per-link certificate and a verifying client bridge. Mux controls appear only for mux transports.
methods.gre: Adjust packet size and IP headers on both GRE interfaces. MTU must also fit your network path; a lower value can help avoid fragmentation.
methods.rathole: Choose TCP, Noise, TLS, WS or WSS. Noise pins the server key. TLS and WSS use managed, verifying TLS bridges; TCP and WS do not encrypt traffic.
methods.reverse_ssh: Tune the managed SSH client. Host verification stays enabled; your management SSH daemon is not changed.
methods.frp_wss: Choose TCP, KCP, QUIC, WebSocket or WSS. Every option verifies the managed TLS certificate. WebSocket carries TLS inside WebSocket; WSS carries WebSocket inside TLS.
methods.hysteria2: Tune QUIC receive windows, timers, and optional Salamander obfuscation. TLS verification stays enabled. Larger buffers consume more memory.

tls.verified_native: TLS certificate and server name are verified against this link’s managed identity. No domain or certificate upload is required.
tls.verified_bridge: MeshDock installs an owned TLS bridge that verifies the peer certificate and server name. Plaintext stays on loopback; TLS protects the connection between servers.

advanced.dualProtocol: This transport also opens a TCP control listener. MeshDock checks both TCP and UDP on this port and restricts access to the peer server.
advanced.architectureLimit: The pinned upstream binary supports this transport on {{architectures}} only. Unsupported servers are rejected before changes are applied.

deployment.cancelling: Cancellation requested. Waiting for the current server operation, then restoring the previous configuration. Do not shut down the worker.
deployment.inspect: Review the server and the last failed step below.

outcome.failed: This revision was not deployed. Previous managed configurations were restored. Edit the connection and deploy again.
outcome.retrying: This attempt failed and was rolled back. MeshDock will retry automatically; you can cancel the retry.
outcome.recovery_required: Rollback could not be confirmed on every server. Restore management access, then select Recover. New deployments remain blocked.
outcome.cancelled: Deployment stopped. Activated changes were rolled back; saved connections remain available to edit or remove.

removal.title: Unfinished removal
removal.explanation: This connection belongs to the last successfully applied configuration. It stays visible until removal succeeds or you restore it. This is deployment history, not a live connectivity check.
removal.uncertain: Rollback has not finished on every server. This connection may still be deployed; its current state is uncertain.
removal.retryHint: Retry deployment of the current requested configuration, including other pending changes. The connection remains visible until removal succeeds.
removal.restoreHint: Put this connection and any missing endpoint servers back into the requested configuration using its original settings. Queue reconciliation, including any other pending changes.
removal.recoverFirst: Complete recovery in the deployment panel before retrying or restoring.
removal.wait: Wait for the current deployment to finish.

sshJump.title: SSH connection path
sshJump.hint: Use another SSH server to reach this server. Only management traffic uses this path; tunnel traffic keeps its configured route. The jump host must permit TCP forwarding to the target SSH port.
sshJump.reuse: Use a saved server, or enter a custom jump host below
sshJump.trust: I verified this jump-host fingerprint independently.

forceDelete.title: Force delete {{name}}
forceDelete.hint: MeshDock will check this server and every connected endpoint, and clean its tunnel connections wherever SSH is available. If only this server is unreachable, it will be forgotten after its peers are cleaned.
forceDelete.preserve: Other connections on shared servers are preserved. Completed cleanup stays in place. Unreachable peers require a separate choice; failed cleanup can be retried.
forceDelete.acknowledge: I understand that forcing deletion may leave resources on this unreachable server.
forceDelete.progressHint: Cleanup is tracked separately for each endpoint. Closing this window does not stop the operation.
forceDelete.queued: Waiting for the worker to check endpoints…
forceDelete.skipHint: Forget this server and its connections without cleaning the unreachable endpoints? Tunnel services and firewall rules may remain there. MeshDock will retain a warning and the cleanup record.
forceDelete.orphans: Deletion completed with skipped cleanup. Resources may remain on the listed endpoints; remove them before reusing or reconnecting those hosts.
forceDelete.missingServer: Server permanently deleted or unreachable? Force deletion checks and cleans its remaining peers.
forceDelete.needsReview: Force deletion needs your attention — review endpoint cleanup

board.hideHint: Remove this card from the board; keep the server in the inventory.
board.locked: Connected servers and SSH jump endpoints must stay on the board.
board.inventoryHint: Move unused cards to inventory. Click or drag them onto the board to bring them back.
board.hiddenNotice: Card moved to inventory. No deployment started.
board.shownNotice: Card added to the board. No deployment started.
board.oneHop: MeshDock connects directly to the jump host, then to this server. A saved server’s own jump route is not followed. Reciprocal routes work only when both jump hosts are directly reachable from MeshDock.

mappingProtocolUnsupported: This mapping protocol is not supported by the selected method or transport. Change the protocol or select a compatible transport.
udpForwardingHint: TCP uses HAProxy. UDP uses native transport listeners or GRE packet forwarding. UDP rows cannot share entry ports with another UDP connection.
